newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Turkmen gas planned to reach Pakistan by year 2001.
newsitem.headline: Turkmen gas planned to reach Pakistan by year 2001.

text.p: The Central Asian republic of Turkmenistan will begin pumping gas to Pakistan through Afghanistan by the year 2001 under an agreement signed on Wednesday by the two countries with proposed pipeline builders.

Pakistan and Turkmenistan signed the agreement in Islamabad with Unocal Corp of the United States and Saudi Arabia's Delta oil company, major partners in a planned consortium to build the $2 billion gas pipeline, Pakistani officials said.

The agreement, signed at the end of a two-day visit by Turkmen Deputy Prime Minister and Oil and Gas Minister Batyr Sardjaev, sets out a schedule for the project, which has been held up by the prolonged civil war in Afghanistan.

A senior Unocal official said last month that while Pakistan and Turkmenistan had demonstrated inter-government support for the project through various agreements, all major factions in Afghanistan, including the dominant Taleban Islamic movement, had also signed project support agreements or letters.
On Wednesday, the signatories agreed to finalise the price of the gas by September 15 and form the consortium by October.
The consortium will secure finances for the project by October 1998, begin construction by the end of 1998 and deliver gas by the year 2001, it said.
Unocal will lead the pipeline consortium, which will also include the Turkmen government, Russia's Gazprom gas company and one or more companies each from Pakistan and Japan.

The official APP news agencyh quoted Pakistan Petroleum and Natural Resources Minister Nisar Ali Khan as saying at the agreement signing ceremony that the gas pipeline project would change the fate of entire region.
"It will set a trend for future projects of telecommunication, power transmission, road links with Central Asian republics and oil supply from Central Asia to the South Asian markets," he said.
Sardjaev said the project would ensure smooth, clean and uninterrupted supply of fuel to Pakistan.

Unocal says the final terms of an arrangement for the passage of the pipeline through Afghanistan against payment of a transit fee can be negotiated only with a stable and internationally recognised government.

The 48-inch (121.92 cm) pipeline is planned to extend 1,464 km (910 miles) from the Daulatabad gas field in southeastern Turkmenistan to the southern Pakistani city of Multan, with about 750 km (466 miles) of it crossing through Afghanistan.
A future 640-km (400-mile) extension to a terminus near the Indian capital, New Delhi, is also possible.
